extracted.intended_audience: tech-news readers and industry watchers (readers of The Register)
extracted.subtask_description: A news/opinion piece reporting on incidents where an AI-generated headline/notification summary produced incorrect or misleading information, evaluating the vendor response and recommended mitigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear labeling of AI-generated summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Software update will 'further clarify' when the text being displayed is summarization provided by Apple Intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it very clear when Apple Intelligence is producing a summary and when content comes directly from an application. Explicit labeling should distinguish AI summaries from publisher or app-originated text to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opt-in delivery of summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Receiving the summaries was optional, but the article argues that Apple should make this an opt in feature until issues have been ironed out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer opt-in defaults for new AI-generated notifications/summaries rather than delivering them to all users by default while accuracy problems persist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate source attribution (avoid misattributing to publishers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The feature generated a headline summary falsely claiming a fact and the summary was attributed to BBC News, prompting a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure AI-generated summaries are not attributed to third-party publishers or presented as if they originate from those publishers; label source clearly to prevent misattribution and legal/reputational complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human fact-checking or temporary removal until fixed
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece criticizes Apple for choosing a software-clarification fix instead of temporarily removing the technology or employing fact-checkers who might ensure accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider human review / fact-checking for high-risk outputs, or suspend problematic features until reliability is demonstrated. Avoid relying solely on superficial UI labels as the only mitigation for substantive inaccuracies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide accessible user reporting mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple encouraged users to report a concern if they view an unexpected notification summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement simple, visible ways for users to report incorrect AI summaries and ensure reported issues are triaged and acted on; use reporting as part of feedback loop but not as a primary safety control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beta disclosure and iterative improvement with user feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple told the BBC: 'Apple Intelligence features are in beta and we are continuously making improvements with the help of user feedback.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly flag experimental features as beta and establish processes to iterate based on user feedback and measured failure modes rather than hiding issues behind banners or vague statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid factual fabrications and time-sensitive errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: AI summarised that Luke Littler had 'won the PDC World Darts Championship hours before it began' and that Rafael Nadal 'had come out as gay'—both inaccurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent premature or fabricated factual claims in summaries, especially for time-sensitive events and sensitive personal information. Validate claims against authoritative sources before surfacing them as facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate AI summaries from application content
rubrics_metrics.description: The article stresses clarifying when content is AI-produced vs. coming directly from an app's notification or publisher feed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design UI/UX to clearly separate AI-generated summaries from native app content (visual cues, labels, provenance metadata), so users can gauge trust and origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage reputational and trust risk from inaccurate AI output
rubrics_metrics.description: If Apple does not make clear distinctions and prevent inaccuracies, it risks being 'spattered by the same AI slop' seen elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat AI-generated misinformation as a brand/trust risk: prioritize reliability, conservative defaults, and corrective processes to avoid damaging user trust and publisher relationships.
